presentation.label: Pitch readout on UP + TEMPO
presentation.summary: Hold UP and press TEMPO to read the selected audio track’s note, octave, cents and frequency in a tuner window.
presentation.overview: Tuner reads the selected audio track after its effects and before its fader. Its note, octave, cents, frequency and needle are designed to help tune a steady pitched sound. It uses no effect slot. This draft offers card builds only; emulator captures of the card build of this source show live readings of a tone on the input; hardware qualification is pending.
highlights: UP then TEMPO opens and closes the tuner window.
Follows the selected audio track; no effect slot or parameter assignment.
Fixed A4 = 440 Hz, with a cents needle and frequency readout.
Source behavior retains the last reading when the signal is too quiet or uncertain.
usage: Include Tuner in a reviewed build and select an audio track with a steady pitched sound. No effect slot is required.
Hold UP first, then press TEMPO. The tuner window shows the selected track, note, octave, cents and frequency.
Adjust the sound at its source while watching the needle. Near the centre the measured pitch approaches the displayed note, with A4 fixed at 440 Hz.
Press TEMPO, YES or NO to close the window. Hold UP and press TEMPO again to toggle it back on.

limitations: Built and emulator-measured on 30 Oct 2026 (card d4452bbb, bus da2375cf) from Tim's v2.21 source plus his DC-removal commit (03202050 that day; ef6cbc7 in his released 2.22 line, the same tuner/ files); the seven older UI screenshots belong to the earlier v2.19/card-sdk image.
The signal is taken after track effects and before the track fader. It is a monophonic pitch estimate; complex, noisy or inharmonic sounds can wander or select an octave.
Below the signal or confidence threshold, the last valid reading is held. A held reading does not indicate the current pitch.
A4 is fixed at 440 Hz. No calibration control, parameter locks, LFO destination or saved project setting is added.
Hold UP before TEMPO. Pressing TEMPO first follows the ordinary tempo-window path.
Card builds only: the base has no removal refusal for ordinary modules.

Sample memory: on a card build without another DRAM module, choosing the Tuner gives up 10,487,808 bytes (about 10.5 MB) of Flex sample RAM. Its own unit is 33 KB, but it is the module that creates the DRAM platform reserve, and the unit sits inside it. Alongside another DRAM module the reserve is shared and the Tuner takes no further sample RAM.
The retained older emulator fault is in its DSP write callback; the triggering image property remains unresolved.

Emulator readings (29 and 30 October 2026) for the figures; on hardware the author reports the TEST3 card (d4452bbb, byte-identical to TEST2) working on his MKI on 1 November 2026, every item of its test sheet, readings not recorded. No hardware timing is measured. The standalone 2.19 reference exited before capture, so paired visual equivalence with it is unavailable.

The reading follows the last 93 ms of the track after its effects, so an effect tail can pull it just after a note changes (on the emulator: E2 +25c 2.4 s after 440 Hz gave way to 82.41 Hz on T8, +0c at 12 s; the same with and without the DC removal).

storage.label: ColdFire code, data and stack
storage.display: 33,130 B of its own (+ the 10.46 MB DRAM platform reserve)
storage.conditions: Exact layout of the card build d4452bbb: 2,894 B code and tables (a local link of upstream/tuner.s compared equal to emulated RAM), 19,500 B state, ring and detector workspace, an 8,194 B unused gap the link leaves between them (.data at 0x40a98130), 2,288 B platform loader and packed unit appended to the image, 18 B of rewritten hook sites and a measured 236 B UI-task stack peak. Any DRAM module also creates the platform reserve taken from Flex sample RAM (10,457,220 B beyond the unit); see TESTING.md.

processing.label: ColdFire, per audio block (amortised)
processing.display: 7,018 of 9,577 cycles per block worst case
processing.conditions: Window open on a pitched tone with the tuner-load8 fixture playing: 195 instructions in the frame interrupt every block, plus one analysis and redraw in the UI task every 400 blocks (1,048,251 instructions at most, 9.9 ms at 9.44 ns per instruction, including the DC-removal pass), amortised over those 400 blocks; window closed: 4 instructions per block. Instruction-count model at 264 MHz, not chip timing; see TESTING.md.

impact.conditions: One open tuner on the selected audio track. Estimates describe source structure, not measured hardware headroom.

cpu.rationale: A bounded sample-copy hook runs each audio block while open; the UI task periodically performs autocorrelation and pitch refinement. Current worst-case cycles and scheduling impact are unmeasured.

dsp.rationale: No DSP program, effect slot or DSP state is added. The tuner reads the existing audio read-back arena.

memory.rationale: One global sample ring and detector workspace; no per-track allocation or new sample storage. Current linked allocation, loader overhead and stack maximum are unmeasured.

tests.summary: Emulator qualification of the card build of this source (card d4452bbb, bus da2375cf) on 30 October 2026: a sine on the input reaches the tap and reads A4 +0c 440.0Hz, E2 +0c 82.4Hz, A4 +19c 445.0Hz and A2 -1c 109.9Hz live, the same as the 29 October build; a fixture track whose signal sits on a DC offset larger than its swing, which held before, now reads (F4, 343-345 Hz, matching an off-line analysis of the same samples); worst-case ColdFire cost 195 instructions per block in the frame interrupt and 1,048,251 per analysis in the UI task (7,018 of 9,577 cycles per block amortised); exact memory with a measured stack peak. The author reports the TEST3 card (the same bytes, rebuilt on current main) working on his MKI on 1 November 2026, every item of its test sheet; readings were not recorded (TESTING.md).
gates: Emulator: tone on the input reaches the read-back tap; 440, 82.41, 445 and 110 Hz read within one cent (LCD captures), unchanged from the build without DC removal
Emulator: a track with a DC offset larger than its AC level reads instead of holding (LCD capture, off-line reference)
Emulator: instruction counts per block (frame hook) and per analysis (UI task) under the tuner-load8 fixture, window open and closed
Unit layout of the card build compared with emulated RAM, and measured UI-task stack peak (exact memory)
Hardware report for this source and image (TEST3 = TEST2, d4452bbb...): timhastie, MKI, 2026-11-01 (reported; TESTING.md)

conditions.parameterExtremes: The Tuner has no parameters. Its branches were all driven: closed window (4 instructions per hook), open window not due (7), analysis rejected at the input gate (silence, max 106,443 per update: the snapshot and the DC-removal pass run before the gate), rejected at the clarity gate (white noise, 972,901), and accepted readings at 82.41, 110, 440 and 445 Hz and on a DC-offset track (max 1,048,251 per update at 440 Hz). Instruction counts on ot_emu c81d13dc for the card image d4452bbb, converted at 9.44 ns per instruction at 264 MHz (2.49216 cycles per instruction); see TESTING.md.
conditions.parameterModulation: No parameter, lock, LFO, scene or MIDI CC path: the module reads only the selected-track byte and the read-back arena. Changing the track while open (T8 -> T2 -> T8) was exercised; the frame hook cost is constant (195 instructions, min = max over 104,872 blocks).
conditions.modeSwitching: Opening (UP + TEMPO to the first draw, 13,749 instructions in the key task from tu_tempo) and closing (TEMPO, 5,968) are one-off events outside the frame path; open, close and reopen were repeated with the fixture playing. Transport start/stop does not change the module's cost (stopped: 195 per block, 1,046,788 per update).
conditions.maxLoad: One global instance. The tuner-load8 fixture playing: seven FLEX tracks with stock FX1 and FX2 on all eight tracks, trigs and retrigs on every track at 120 BPM, T8 THRU on input A. Per block: 195 instructions in the frame interrupt plus the UI-task analysis and redraw (1,048,251 instructions at most, every 400 blocks, preempted by the frame interrupt) amortised over 400 blocks plus 108 not-due visits a second at 7: 2,816 instructions = 7,018 cycles, against Modwerk's 9,577-cycle ColdFire allowance (10 % of a 362.8 us block at 264 MHz). The frame-interrupt share alone is 486 cycles. UI-task counts exclude nested frame-interrupt bodies and include any other interrupt (upper bound). No USB or MIDI traffic was driven.
conditions.inputConditions: Sines at 0.5 FS on the input (82.41, 110, 440, 445 Hz), white noise and silence through T8 THRU and the track's effects to the read-back tap; a FLEX track whose signal after its effects sits on a DC offset larger than its swing (reads F4, 343-345 Hz). The pitched path is the most expensive (YIN refinement runs only on an accepted lobe); the noise path stops after the lag loop and the silent path after the DC-removal pass.

regions.name: Tuner DRAM unit code and tables (.text)
Tuner state, sample ring, snapshot and detector workspace (.data)
Unused link gap between .text and .data inside the unit span
Platform loader and packed Tuner unit appended to the image
Three hook sites rewritten in place (3 x 6-byte detours)
UI-task caller stack below the loop head (measured peak, tu_tick + tu_draw + stock text routine)
Platform reserve: Flex sample RAM given up to the DRAM platform, less the unit span

memory.conditions: Exact layout of the card build d4452bbb (bus da2375cf): the unit's 2,894-byte .text compared equal to a local link of upstream/tuner.s at 0x40a955e0 with .data at 0x40a98130; the 2,288 bytes appended to the bus. The Tuner's own bytes are 33,130: 2,894 code and tables, 19,500 data (state 44, ring 8,192, snapshot 8,192, decimated 2,048, NSDF 740, lobes 256, YIN 28), the 8,194-byte gap the link leaves between them, 2,288 appended loader and packed unit, 18 bytes of hook sites, and a 236-byte UI-task stack peak measured on the emulator (own frames 172 B static; the DC-removal pass uses registers only). The frame hook uses no stack. The 10,457,220-byte platform reserve is Flex sample RAM given up to the DRAM platform (10,487,808 B less the unit span); any DRAM module creates it. No heap, SRAM, battery-RAM or DSP allocation; the window is the stock TEMPO window object. No hardware canary was measured.

hardware.summary: The author flashed OCTATRACK_MODWERK_TUNER_TEST3.bin (448,084 B, sha256 d4452bbb..., byte-identical to TEST2) on his Octatrack MKI on 1 November 2026 and reported the TEST3 sheet passing (his words, one line for three sheets: 'tuner ... pass'). The sheet's checks: a pitched source on the selected track (a THRU track on input A, or a pitched sample); UP held first then TEMPO opens the TUNER window with the track number, TEMPO first opens the stock tempo window; a steady note reads its note, octave, cents and frequency with the needle centred in tune; a sharp note moves the needle right with +cents and a flat note left with -cents, the reading updating about seven times a second and still on a steady note; when the signal stops the last reading stays with HOLD in the header and HOLD goes away on playing; the DC case (EQ and CHORUS on a track playing a sustained pitched sample) reads a note instead of HOLD; the header follows the track keys; TEMPO, YES, NO or UP + TEMPO close the window and TEMPO alone and FUNC + TEMPO keep their stock behaviour; no clicks or dropouts while it is open.
limitations: The readings seen, what was fed in, the DC case's figures and the play time were not recorded; the report is the sheet's pass line, reported by the author and not independently repeated.

A functional check of the sheet's items, not a load or stress run; no hardware timing, stack canary or audio measurement. The cycle figures beside this report are the emulator's instruction-count model.
The MKI only; not run on an MKII.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial: tune a sound on a track
steps: Select the audio track to tune with its track key. Tuner reads the track after its effects and before its fader, so a quiet or faded track still reads.
Hold UP first, then press TEMPO. The window shows the track, the note and octave, a +-50 cent needle, the cents and the frequency.
Play a steady pitched sound on that track (a THRU track with an instrument on input A, or a sample) and adjust it until the needle is centred and the cents read +0c.
Below the signal gate or without a clear pitch the last reading stays with HOLD in the header. Press TEMPO, YES or NO, or UP + TEMPO again, to close the window.
